title: Introduce fragmentation ledger, stripe compactor and fair-share spill reservoir
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Added a fragmentation ledger and stripe-based compactor to reduce KV cache fragmentation; introduced a fair-share spill reservoir to stabilize spill-to-disk under bursty workloads. No user-visible API changes.
description: Motivation: production workloads showed long-tail memory fragmentation in the KV cache when tenants/keys produced many small allocations and transient fragments. Existing evictors reacted to pressure but were unable to compact scattered fragments without expensive full-scan compactions, causing elevated p95 latencies and increased spill events. This PR introduces three complementary subsystems: 1) a lightweight fragmentation ledger that tracks per-tenant fragment histograms and hot-spot indices, 2) a stripe-based incremental compactor that merges small fragments into contiguous stripes during low-util windows, and 3) a fair-share spill reservoir that gates spill-to-disk so tenants cannot trigger global thrashing. Design highlights: - Fragmentation ledger: maintained as a lock-free append-only ring per shard; periodically summarised to compute a fragmentation score per tenant/segment. Ledger entries are compact (16B-ish) to keep telemetry overhead low. - Stripe compactor: compacts at stripe granularity (configurable, default 64KB) and prioritizes high-fragmentation tenants observed by the ledger. Compaction is preemptible and piggybacks on background worker tokens to avoid interfering with latency-critical request paths. - Fair-share spill reservoir: allocates a reservoir budget per tenant and enforces a leaky-bucket style drain to smooth spills. When global available disk bandwidth is low, the reservoir enforces backpressure and requests are routed to alternative fallback model variants where applicable. - Kernel/allocator hints: introduced a compact-on-access hint path so frequently accessed small allocations are preferentially relocated into compaction-friendly slabs. - Telemetry & ops: added metrics (kv.fragmentation_score, kv.stripe_compactions, kv.spill_reservoir_usage) and dashboards; created a diagnostic dump for offline analysis. Checklist: - [x] Ledger core implementation and unit tests - [x] Stripe compactor worker + integration tests - [x] Fair-share spill reservoir + e2e tests with synthetic tenants - [x] CI benchmarks and perf regression guardrails - [x] Docs + runbook for tuning compaction windows Backwards compatibility & safety: default behavior is off for stripe compaction and conservative defaults for reservoir quotas. The ledger is read-only telemetry when disabled and has negligible overhead. Benchmarks (internal): - Controlled tenant-mix test (10 tenants, skewed 80/20 accesses): fragmentation score reduced by ~78%; KV cache usable resident set increased ~22% for steady-state workloads. - P99 latency impact during peak: compaction background ramp introduces +0.4ms median and +1.2ms p99 under default token caps; lowering compaction concurrency removes p99 regression at cost of slower defragmentation. - Spill event reduction: synthetic burst test showed 63% fewer spill-to-disk events and 41% lower aggregate spill bandwidth. Trade-offs: compaction uses CPU and memory copy bandwidth; the fairness reservoir can increase tail latency for aggressive tenants but prevents global instability. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-271 and references to prior eviction tuning PRs. See linked Linear items for rollout plan.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) ledger: add fragmentation ledger and ring buffer summarizer (with unit tests), 2) compactor: stripe compactor worker and scheduler + integration harness for low-load windows, 3) reservoir: spill reservoir implementation, docs, dashboards, and e2e test scenarios. Each commit contains focused refactors for allocator hint surfaces.
review_thread: Diego: Can you clarify ledger overhead when there are >1000 tenants on a single shard? Asha: Ledger entries are per-segment; we summarize and rollup at shard-level so memory cost is ~O(segments) not O(tenants). Priya: The compactor preemption looks racy in the first iteration — I saw a test flake where worker tokens weren't released. Asha: Fixed in commit 3, added stronger invariants and a token-leak unit test. Liam: Approve after adding a guard for reservoir config to prevent zero-budget deployment. Diego: CI initial run failed on flaky test test_allocator_hints (timing); rerun passed. Final: LGTM and squash+merge.
notes: Feature guarded behind runtime flags. Ops to enable: set kv.compaction.enabled=true and tune kv.compaction.tokens and kv.spill.reservoir.default_quota. Runbooks added under docs/runbooks.
